__doc__: sim-robust-vram-headroom-default-on-v1 bounded GPU proof + acceptance numbers for the integration lane. This lane flips TWO footprint defaults ON (each opt-out via config) and makes the pre-boot VRAM guard's minimum HONEST (derived from the measured mission peak minus the default-on trims plus a stated margin, naming what holds the memory). The point: a run must boot AND complete on the 12 GiB RTX 3060 with ~2.5 GB already taken by the always-on whispr service (which is NEVER touched). The capstone config needs NO new keys to get the protection now -- it is the DEFAULT. Opt-out lines are below for a controlled A/B. GPU rule unchanged: one run at a time via flock /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, never --force, --heavy-threshold-mb 2500 for whispr, whispr never touched.
_default_on_now: With NO 'vram_headroom' block and NO RESTOCK_STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING env, a run now gets: (1) the VRAM headroom monitor (samples FREE VRAM on the sim clock, sheds optional load by name below floor_mib, names the ceiling) AND (2) the proactive fm380 stage-scoped sensing teardown fired at collect->couple (returns the ~0.95 GB shelf-camera render product BEFORE the long couple->transfer->return creep span). coldwin16 proved both mechanisms under genuine pressure (free fell to 368 MiB at return; the monitor fired capture_rate + secondary_cameras by name and the run COMPLETED, where un-monitored coldwin13 took a native SIGSEGV at the ceiling).

_opt_out_for_an_A_B._note: Set EITHER/BOTH to reproduce the pre-flip behaviour. The env RESTOCK_STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING=0 is an equivalent legacy opt-out for the teardown. Absent => both ON.

_preboot_guard: The honest pre-boot guard is scripts/twin/tools/vram_guard.py. One line (the orchestrator runs it before boot): `python3 scripts/twin/tools/vram_guard.py --config <mission-runtime.json>`. It DERIVES the minimum FREE VRAM from gpu_budget's measured mission footprint (the configured feeds) MINUS the default-on stage-scoped teardown saving (~948 MiB) PLUS a stated margin (default 400 MiB), and its refusal line names the resident holders (whispr) parsed from nvidia-smi. Exit 0 = enough free; exit 6 = refuse (names the derived minimum + its breakdown + what holds the memory). `--margin-mib` tunes the stated margin; `--min-free-mib` overrides (discouraged).

_acceptance_numbers.old_fixed_min: 9500 MiB (removed -- unrelated to any measured peak; refused free=9473 beside 2.44 GB whispr yet was itself below the real ~9630 footprint)
_acceptance_numbers.boots_beside_244gb_whispr: free ~9473 MiB (card 12288 - whispr ~2498 - ~317 other) >= derived 9082 => the honest guard now ADMITS the boot the fixed 9500 wrongly refused
_acceptance_numbers.teardown_opt_out_min: 9544 MiB (no trim => mission needs its full footprint free -- the guard honestly refuses to boot it beside 2.44 GB whispr)
_acceptance_numbers.mast_second_feed_min: 9568 MiB (opt-in mast camera_1 raises the minimum)
_acceptance_numbers.expected_operating_peak_target: coldwin16 peaked 11697 MiB used WITHOUT the proactive teardown (its secondary_cameras shed fired only at RETURN). With the teardown DEFAULT-ON firing at collect->couple, the shelf ~0.95 GB is gone before the creep window => expect the creep peak ~10.7-10.8 GB used (coldwin16 - ~948), i.e. headroom ~1.5 GB above the card floor beside 2.5 GB whispr. The vram_headroom monitor remains the reactive net if the internal RTX allocator creep still brushes the floor.

_run_A_default_on: FULL CAPSTONE with NO vram_headroom/sensing_teardown keys and NO RESTOCK_STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING (= all default-on). PASS = mission.json state=complete; STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING torn down line present at the collect->couple boundary (shelf freed, unless a camera-mode transfer/sensor-verify keeps it); vram_headroom_mode=on in mission.json; vram-headroom.json peak_used recorded; peak_used MiB <= coldwin16's 11697 (expect ~10.7-10.8 GB); whispr untouched; lock released.
_run_B_guard_honest: Pre-boot, with whispr resident at ~2.4-2.5 GB and the card otherwise idle, run `python3 scripts/twin/tools/vram_guard.py --config <capstone-runtime.json>`. PASS = exit 0 with a line like `VRAM_GUARD OK: free=<~9473> MiB >= min 9082 MiB [min = mission peak 9630.0 MiB - teardown 948 MiB + margin 400 MiB]`. Then flip sensing_teardown off in the config and re-run the guard: PASS = exit 6 (or a higher min) naming whispr as the holder (the opt-out config honestly needs more free VRAM).
_run_C_opt_out_byte_identical: Controlled A/B: a staged transfer (start_at=transfer, recorded_bay_park, stop_after=verify) with BOTH opt-outs set (vram_headroom:false + sensing_teardown:{stage_scoped:false}). PASS = state=complete AND no STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING teardown line AND no vram_headroom_mode in mission.json (restores the pre-flip path).

_suggested_env.RESTOCK_RENDER_WIDTH: 960 (unchanged -- render resolution is NOT the VRAM lever, memory mission-vram-ceiling-12gb)
_suggested_env.RESTOCK_STAGE_SCOPED_SENSING: leave UNSET (teardown is default-on via config now); set to 0 only to force the teardown off as a legacy override
